We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{2}{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{2}{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{3}^{x}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }({3}^{2}-{3}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{3}^{a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={3}^{x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{3}^{x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{3}^{x}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067475/assets/abae6131aceb7348a82ea01a544b28a62d8835b7857da14a6339b4ae3b88a1fd.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{3}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-0) \\  & =\frac{9}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}.\end{aligned}
$$
